# What is a Product
## Scrum.org
47400 subscribers
145 likes

### Description
13364 views
Posted: 15 Oct 2020
In this Scrum Tapas video, Professional Scrum Trainer Ralph Jocham tells a story that he uses in his Professional Scrum Product Owner class to help students understand how to define a product and what it takes to describe the product.

3 comments
### Transcript:
[Music] hi my name is rafam and today i would like to talk about what is a product in my scrum and specifically my product owner trainings i very often get the question what actually is a product this is a very important question let me put it that way the challenge of correctly defining your product is one of the most important decisions you will make in our book the professional product owner don mcgrill and i describe a product as something which has a producer and consumer the consumer either is willing to pay or get some cost benefit by using the product and the product solves a problem for the consumer a product does not have to be a physical object a product could also be a material like a service what is your product or what things to consider when defining your product let's say you drove to work in your car this morning these days steering wheels have buttons on them to adjust the volume or initiate a phone call is this button a product absolutely there's a producer and consumer who's bought the buttons and it solves the problem now did you ever buy a button for your steering wheel i guess the answer is no is the steering wheeler product yes absolutely the same criteria apply again now did you ever buy a steering wheel on its own i guess the answer is no unless you are a tinkerer well what do you purchase a car a car is the product which solves an important problem for you transport defining your product is about finding the right level of abstraction usually the larger you go the better it is why let's look at the bank there's an interest calculator component which is considered a product which means there will be a product owner scrum master and development team there is also the account management system which again is a product and yes there's the money wire service transaction logging web front end and so on you get the idea you will have an army of product owners forming a web of dependencies more important where in this picture is the real customer follow the money combine all the components forming the value stream pointing towards the real consumer your customer this value stream is your product here we have her her name is nancy and she wants to buy a house she's looking for a loan the loan is her product the bank is the provider nancy the consumer and it solves the problem all dimension components form the value stream for the loan product in general you can assume that the value stream points outside the boundaries of your company meaning that the consumer is not on your company's payroll the resulting value stream should be guided by a single product vision the guiding beacon for all the components and there will be one product owner the validation of this resulting product also is much more meaningful if the product is large it is common to have several development teams working for this one product owner on that one value stream again the common vision ensures a shared alignment between those teams i strongly believe that every person working on a product should know their place within the value stream what about shared products or components they cannot be eliminated the goal is to minimize them the less chat components you have the more independent and faster your value stream can act the more agile your business can be having products which are defined too small and therefore depending on too many components leads to the following problems a project mindset sequential life cycle and milestones unnecessary dependency management and coordination hand off information scatter and high inventory too much focus on efficiencies working on low value features opaque measure of progress causing invention of work loss of customer and whole product focus cost of delay and finally less value the more your product expands the less shared components you will have and the less of dimension problems it's about scaling the product not your scrum let me summarize managing workers products rather than project changes structures decisions and behaviors in product development which in itself fosters an agile mindset structuring your organization and company around your value stream should be your ultimate goal i'm ralph chokhan i'm also a professional scrum trainer with scrum.org and i would like to invite you to one of my trainings thank you
